issues.body: `claim_ref_slots()` stores refs in a `dict[int, str]`, so distinct valid matches such as `refs/acct-claims/acct1` and `refs/acct-claims/[redacted-account]` both become key `1`; the latter silently overwrites the former. The accepted grammar and the existing allocation readers allow any `[0-9]+`, while git refs themselves are distinct. Consequently `claims=`, `burned=`, and the named rows can omit a real claim ref. This is especially problematic because the function explicitly promises to fail closed on malformed listings and the README says each claim is counted/named. The self-test only supplies unique numeric slots, so it cannot detect the overwrite.
issues.fix_hint: Reject duplicate numeric slot keys (including alternate zero-padding) as an inconsistent/malformed claim inventory, or preserve and report every distinct ref with semantics that cannot silently undercount. Add a test containing both `acct1` and `[redacted-account]` and assert the chosen fail-closed behavior; also verify the CLI exits nonzero and emits no burned-slot report for that inventory.
issues.title: Numerically equivalent claim refs are silently collapsed

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The report is read-only and generally fail-closed, but its claim parser silently collapses distinct claim refs that encode the same integer slot. That contradicts the marquee promise to count/name every burned claim and turns an inconsistent claim namespace into an under-report instead of a refusal. Round 1, so progress is null.
